stories.headline: Eritrea cuts diplomatic ties with Ethiopia after diplomat expulsions and rebel support claims
stories.body:
Eritrea cut all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia on Thursday following a growing political dispute.

The decision came after Ethiopia expelled Eritrean diplomats from its capital, Addis Ababa. Ethiopia declared 10 Eritrean diplomats persona non grata. These diplomats included the charge d'affaires and officials accredited to the African Union. Ethiopia gave the 10 diplomats 48 hours to leave the country.

The official break in diplomatic ties occurred on October 1, 2026. Both countries accused each other of stoking internal conflicts. Ethiopia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt of backing a new rebel alliance. Ethiopia said these countries are supporting an opposition group led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front.

Eritrea denied these claims. Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel said Eritrea is not backing the newly formed rebel alliance. The opposition coalition against Ethiopia's federal government includes several armed groups. It includes the Tigray People's Liberation Front and the Oromo Liberation Army. It also includes a faction of the Ogaden National Liberation Front. Militant groups from Benishangul-Gumuz and Afar have joined the alliance as well.

Fighting has continued to cause civilian deaths in the region. A medic in the southern Tigrayan town of Alamata reported that 52 civilians died during three days of heavy fighting. In response to rising security concerns, Ethiopian security services took new measures. Ethiopia's National Intelligence and Security Service announced an indefinite ban on drone flights. This ban applies to Addis Ababa and surrounding areas.

The conflict comes after a history of long tension and changing relations between the two nations. Ethiopia annexed Eritrea in 1962. Eritrea secured its independence in 1993. President Isaias Afwerki led an armed struggle that won independence for Eritrea. Relations improved when Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed came to power in 2018. Abiy moved to normalise diplomatic relations with President Afwerki.

Later, a major civil war broke out inside Ethiopia. The civil war lasted two years between the Ethiopian federal government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front. An African Union mediator estimated that 600,000 lives were lost during the civil war between 2020 and 2022. The 2022 Pretoria Peace Agreement ended that civil war. Now, new fighting and accusations have broken the peace between the two neighboring countries.

claims.text: Eritrea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Thursday that it was severing all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia in response to the expulsion of its diplomats from Addis Ababa.
Ethiopia declared 10 Eritrean diplomats in Addis Ababa, including the charge d'affaires and diplomats accredited to the African Union, persona non grata and ordered them to leave within 48 hours.
Ethiopia and Eritrea broke diplomatic ties on October 1, 2026, after accusing each other of stoking internal conflicts.
Ethiopia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt of supporting an opposition alliance led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front.
Eritrea's Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel denied that Eritrea was backing the newly formed rebel alliance fighting the Ethiopian government.

An opposition coalition against Ethiopia's federal government includes the Tigray People's Liberation Front, the Oromo Liberation Army, a faction of the Ogaden National Liberation Front, and militant groups from Benishangul-Gumuz and Afar.
A medic in the southern Tigrayan town of Alamata reported that 52 civilians died during three days of heavy fighting.
Ethiopia's National Intelligence and Security Service announced an indefinite ban on drone flights in Addis Ababa and surrounding areas.
Ethiopia annexed Eritrea in 1962, and Eritrea secured independence in 1993 following an armed struggle led by President Isaias Afwerki.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed moved to normalise diplomatic relations with Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki when Abiy came to power in 2018.
The 2022 Pretoria Peace Agreement ended a two-year civil war between the Ethiopian federal government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front.
An African Union mediator estimated that 600,000 lives were lost during the civil war in Ethiopia between 2020 and 2022.

stories.headline: French prime minister holds crisis meeting as student protests cause widespread violence
stories.body:
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu held a crisis meeting on Thursday over spreading student unrest.

Nationwide high school protests led to violence and major disruptions. French police arrested 1,949 people during the protests on Thursday. The police reported that 305 police officers suffered injuries. France's interior ministry said student actions affected 1,027 out of 3,700 high schools across the country. Students set up blockades at 222 high schools. University students joined the demonstrations on Thursday and blocked access to about 30 university campuses.

Protests turned violent in several cities. A bin fire at Nelson Mandela high school in Nantes damaged the entrance hall. In Auchel, the headteacher at Degrugillier high school suffered an ear injury from a firework. Protesters outside Saint-Exupery high school in Marseille forced firefighters to leave their vehicle before setting the fire truck on fire. Authorities in Strasbourg ordered tram services to halt after students placed barriers on the tracks.

French National Rally leader Marine Le Pen called for a new anti-rioting law. Le Pen said the protests were riots organised by professionals and overseen by deputies from La France Insoumise. The French government announced that many high schools would switch to online classes. Education Minister Édouard Geffray scheduled meetings for Friday with unions, parent groups, and student associations. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez launched an internal police investigation over allegations of excessive force against three students.

claims.text: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu held a crisis meeting on Thursday to address escalating student unrest across the country.
French police arrested 1,949 people and reported 305 police officers injured during nationwide high school protests on Thursday.
France's interior ministry reported that 1,027 out of 3,700 high schools across the country were affected by student actions, including blockades at 222 schools.
University students in France joined the high school demonstrations on Thursday, blocking access to about 30 university campuses.
A bin fire at the Nelson Mandela high school in Nantes spread to the front of the building and damaged the entrance hall.
The headteacher at Degrugillier high school in Auchel sustained an ear injury from a firework during student protests.
Protesters outside Saint-Exupery high school in Marseille forced firefighters to flee their vehicle before setting the fire truck on fire.
Regional prefect authorities in Strasbourg ordered tram services to halt after protesting students placed barriers on the tracks.
French National Rally leader Marine Le Pen called for a new anti-rioting law, stating that the protests were "riots organized by professionals and overseen by deputies from La France Insoumise."
The French government announced that many high schools would switch to online classes due to safety concerns from ongoing student protests.
French Education Minister Édouard Geffray scheduled meetings for Friday with representative staff unions, parent groups, and student associations.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez launched an internal police investigation following allegations of excessive force and brutality against three students.

stories.headline: United States urges European allies to release emergency fuel reserves as prices surge
stories.body:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged European partners on social media to release emergency diesel reserves immediately.

Fuel prices surged after the start of the US war on Iran. Average US diesel prices rose over 70 percent to $6.39 per gallon. US President Donald Trump said he is considering a ban on US diesel exports to lower domestic costs. European Union trade chief Maros Sefcovic warned that an export ban would bring dramatic economic consequences. Sefcovic said such a ban would be unexpected for Europeans.

In the United Kingdom, the average price of a litre of diesel reached a record 199.72p on Wednesday. Brent crude oil prices rose above $101 per barrel on Thursday. Prices stood at about $72 a barrel in February before the Iran war. British ministers held calls on Thursday with European partners to discuss using emergency reserves. French President Emmanuel Macron planned a G7 meeting for mid-October to coordinate fuel releases.

Other nations took steps to protect domestic fuel supplies. PetroChina cancelled October fuel shipments beyond Hong Kong and Macau. Russia extended its diesel export ban through October 31. Refined product shipments through the Strait of Hormuz dropped sharply to 677,000 barrels per day in late September. Tensions in the strait remained high after three oil tankers were struck by projectiles on Tuesday.

claims.text: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged European partners on social media to immediately release strategic diesel reserves to address supply disruptions.
Average US diesel prices surged over 70 percent to $6.39 per gallon following the start of the US war on Iran, according to AAA data.
US President Donald Trump stated he was considering a potential ban on US diesel exports to curb domestic fuel costs.
European Union trade chief Maros Sefcovic warned that any US ban on diesel exports would be "unexpected for Europeans" and cause "very dramatic consequences" for economic performance.
The average price of a litre of diesel in the United Kingdom reached a record high of 199.72p on Wednesday, according to the RAC.
Brent crude oil prices rose above $101 per barrel on Thursday, up from about $72 a barrel in February prior to the Iran war.
British ministers held calls on Thursday with counterparts from the European Commission, Germany, France, Italy, and Ireland to discuss drawing down emergency diesel reserves.
French President Emmanuel Macron planned a video meeting of G7 leaders for mid-October to discuss coordinating releases of fuel reserves.
PetroChina cancelled October shipments of gasoline and jet fuel to destinations beyond Hong Kong and Macau to protect domestic supplies.
Russia extended its export ban on diesel for fuel producers through October 31 to maintain domestic fuel market stability.
Kpler recorded that refined product shipments through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 677,000 barrels per day in late September, down from 3.6 million barrels per day before the Iran war.
Three Liberian-flagged oil tankers were struck by projectiles on Tuesday while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Indian pilot praised after surviving cockpit stabbing on Flydubai flight as UAE probes terror link
stories.body:
Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar survived a knife attack inside the cockpit on a flight carrying 174 passengers.

His co-pilot attacked him with a knife during the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The attack forced the flight to make an emergency landing in Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia on Wednesday. The plane was Flydubai flight FZ1073. It landed safely in Tabuk at 9:45 am local time with 174 passengers and eight crew members.

According to Flightradar24, the aircraft plummeted around 17,000 feet in altitude in one minute during the fight. Media reports said 166 of the 174 passengers were Israeli citizens. The suspect accused of attacking the captain is an Omani national. Machchhar was transferred to Abu Dhabi to recover from his injuries.

World leaders praised the Indian pilot for his bravery. US President Donald Trump called Machchhar a hero for fighting off the attacker and opening the cockpit door to call for help. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on X that Machchhar showed immense courage. Modi added that Machchhar's quick actions prevented another attack like 9/11. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu praised Machchhar on X for saving 174 lives and preventing a disaster. Netanyahu said the co-pilot had undergone Islamist radical indoctrination.

Saudi Arabia's interior ministry said the co-pilot was transferred to the United Arab Emirates on Thursday morning. An Emirati security team accompanied the co-pilot during the transfer. The UAE chief prosecutor announced an investigation into the fight. UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi launched an official probe into whether the attack involved terrorist intent. Authorities from Saudi Arabia, Israel, the UAE, the US, and Oman are jointly working to determine the motive. Israeli intelligence and security officials traveled to Saudi Arabia to help with the investigation.

US President Donald Trump said Tehran was likely involved in the flight attack. Trump warned that Iran would be hit very hard if it was responsible. Trump also said in an interview with Time magazine that he might resume bombing Iran after November 3. The Wall Street Journal reported that the US plans to send up to 10,000 extra troops to the Middle East. The US will also send a third aircraft carrier by late November. All 174 passengers later continued their journey to Tel Aviv on a replacement plane. They departed Saudi Arabia at approximately 5:40 pm on Wednesday.

claims.text: Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar survived a knife attack by his co-pilot inside the cockpit on a flight carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
The cockpit attack forced the Flydubai flight to make an emergency landing in Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia on Wednesday.
Saudi Arabia's Interior Ministry stated that Flydubai flight FZ1073 landed safely in Tabuk at 9:45 am local time with 174 passengers and eight crew members on board.
According to Flightradar24, the Flydubai flight plummeted around 17,000 feet in altitude in the span of a minute during the cockpit altercation.
Media reports indicated that 166 out of the 174 passengers aboard the Flydubai flight were Israeli citizens.
The co-pilot accused of attacking the captain is an Omani national.
Captain Smit Machchhar was transferred to Abu Dhabi to recover from his injuries.
US President Donald Trump praised Captain Smit Machchhar as a hero for fighting off the knife attack and opening the cockpit door to call for help.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated on X that Captain Smit Machchhar showed immense courage and that his quick actions prevented another 9/11-like attack.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu posted on X praising Captain Smit Machchhar for preventing a catastrophic midair disaster and saving 174 lives.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that the co-pilot behind the attack on the Flydubai flight had undergone Islamist radical indoctrination.
Saudi Arabia's interior ministry stated that the co-pilot was transferred to the United Arab Emirates on Thursday morning accompanied by an Emirati security team.
The UAE chief prosecutor announced an investigation into the Flydubai cockpit fight, including the possibility of terrorist activity or intent.
UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi launched an official investigation into whether the cockpit attack involved terrorist intent or prior planning.
Authorities from Saudi Arabia, Israel, the UAE, the United States, and Oman are jointly involved in efforts to determine the motive behind the Flydubai attack.
Israeli intelligence and security officials traveled to Saudi Arabia to assist with the investigation into the Flydubai flight incident.
US President Donald Trump stated that Tehran was likely involved in the Flydubai flight attack and warned that Iran would be hit very hard if it was responsible.
In an interview published by Time magazine, US President Donald Trump stated it was possible he might resume bombing Iran after the US midterm elections on November 3.
The Wall Street Journal reported that the United States was set to send a third aircraft carrier and up to 10,000 extra service members to the Middle East by late November.
All 174 passengers from the diverted Flydubai flight continued their journey to Tel Aviv at approximately 5:40 pm on Wednesday on a replacement aircraft.

stories.headline: Election Commission orders probe into bulk voter deletion applications in Karnataka
stories.body:
The Election Commission of India ordered an investigation into bulk voter deletion filings in Karnataka.

The decision followed a five-hour protest by Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar. Chief Electoral Officer of Karnataka V. Anbu Kumar directed officials to take action against false Form-7 filings. Karnataka Police registered five cases on October 1, 2026, over the bulk filings. Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi accused the BJP and election officials of colluding to delete targeted voters. Reports showed that many voter deletion filings targeted Muslim voters during the Special Intensive Revision.

In Babaleshwar, 10 individuals submitted 1,363 out of 1,373 Form 7 applications on September 22. In Bhalki, 30 people filed over 1,700 deletion applications on September 23. Political pressure against election officials grew across India. Leaders from 21 Opposition parties met in New Delhi on September 30 to plan strategy against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke called Kumar a puppet of government leaders. Dipke claimed that about 13 crore voters have been deleted from electoral rolls since 2024. The Cockroach Janta Party demanded that future elections use paper ballots instead of electronic voting machines. The Election Commission dismissed claims of internal breakdown and said all commissioners agreed on key decisions.

claims.text: The Election Commission of India ordered a probe into bulk Form-7 voter deletion filings following a five-hour protest by Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar.

Chief Electoral Officer of Karnataka V. Anbu Kumar directed Electoral Registration Officers to act against applicants submitting false Form-7 voter deletion claims under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Karnataka Police registered five FIRs on October 1, 2026, over bulk Form-7 filings under the Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita, 2023.
Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi stated that BJP and Election Commission officials colluded to fill out Form-7s in bulk to delete targeted voters.
According to a report by The Hindu, a majority of the 4,000 Form 7 voter deletion applications filed during Karnataka's Special Intensive Revision targeted Muslim voters.
In Vijayapura district's Babaleshwar constituency, 1,363 out of 1,373 Form 7 applications filed on September 22 were submitted by just 10 individuals.
In Bhalki in Bidar district, 30 individuals submitted over 1,700 Form 7 voter deletion applications on September 23.
Leaders from 21 Opposition parties met in New Delhi on September 30 to outline a joint strategy against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke called Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar a puppet of Amit Shah and Narendra Modi during a press conference in Mumbai on October 1, 2026.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke claimed that approximately 13 crore voters have been deleted from Indian electoral rolls since 2024.
The Cockroach Janta Party demanded that future Indian elections be conducted using paper ballots rather than Electronic Voting Machines.
The Election Commission of India dismissed claims of an internal breakdown, stating all three commissioners were in agreement on decisions regarding the Special Intensive Revision.

vocab.meaning: secretly cooperating for an illegal or dishonest purpose
